why does a cricket ball swing through the air

Look at a used ball: one side is polished shiny, the other stays rough. ✨ Air slides smoothly over the shiny side but tumbles over the rough one, and that difference pushes the ball off its straight line, usually towards the rough side. That is why fielders keep polishing one half on their trousers. 🏏
[CHIPS]What is reverse swing|Why new balls swing[/CHIPS]

why do teenagers need more sleep than kids

Small correction first: teenagers actually need slightly less than younger children, roughly eight to ten hours against nine to twelve for a nine year old. What really changes is the timing. At puberty your body clock shifts later, melatonin is released later in the evening, and falling asleep at nine gets genuinely hard while school still starts early. That mismatch, not laziness, is why teenagers are exhausted. 😴[CHIPS]What is melatonin|Can i catch up|Something else[/CHIPS]

why do people freeze in an emergency instead of acting

Freezing is not cowardice, it is a search. Your brain reaches for a stored plan that matches what it is seeing, and when it finds nothing it keeps searching while the seconds run. That is why drills work: they plant a plan you can grab without thinking. Notice the exits in a new cinema or a new classroom, and half the work is already done. 🧠

why do people sprinkle salt on icy roads

Salt lowers the temperature at which water freezes. Dissolved salt particles keep getting in the way of water molecules trying to lock into an ice crystal, so the ice needs to be colder than usual to hold together — and at ordinary winter temperatures it melts instead. In a deep enough freeze, though, plain salt stops helping. ❄️
